pass_a_gloss: …very wisely recorded, upon it not being possible for the crowds to come together with him, but only those differing beside the crowds, who were his disciples, and able to have boldness toward entering into the house of Jesus. There, not as those who are outside, but having room to become inside, coming toward the teacher, they think it right to learn the inner mind of the parables. And since they had room to follow him entering into the house, for this reason answering toward Explain to us the parable, he said the things he said. And Jesus not only goes out of his own house, in order that having become outside he may speak the parables to those outside, but he also sits beside the sea, hinting that the crowds and those outside are not far from the waves of the sea and from its salty water. And keep watch that toward Jesus who went out of the house and sat beside the sea many crowds were gathered; yet no longer many crowds, but the few traveling the narrow and pressed way, and finding the road that leads into life, disciples, enter toward him into the house. Examining then by a word what is fitting to a gospel according to power, and to the intention of Jesus who embarked into the boat and speaks in parables to every crowd beside the shore, I say: perhaps the Word, not having stepped, nor standing, but being in sea-water, speaks carried upon that which, as far as possible, is able to have stepped upon water — which has been called a boat. And do not wonder if such thoughts have been brought in more beautifully, so that the one outside and the crowd may not suppose there is no mind at all hidden and holding dense elegance that lies stored for the gospel disposition; for it was also a work of the grace that manages the Word of God. And I also try to hear more deeply Coming forward the disciples said to him: Why do you speak to them in parables? and Leaving the crowds he came into his own house; and his disciples came toward him saying: Explain to us the parable. For always the crowds, if they hear a parable, do not even attend to it as needing explanation; but the disciples, seeing that he speaks in parables to the crowds because they are outside, follow Jesus as he leaves the crowds, and seeing that they cannot learn the things of the parables elsewhere than by entering into the house of Jesus, they also enter toward him, and coming toward him they say: Explain to us the parable about which they wish to learn. But such is the parable. Next is the dark saying. There are, then, in the Scriptures some things said so purposely darkly that one could not take even the chance meaning in them apart from much and great examination confused both according to the phrasing and according to the thought and according to the composition of the wording; which I think is the so-called dark saying in a book. I will set out an example of such things from Psalms, from Psalm 32, the things said thus: Because I was silent, my bones grew old, and the things following. And simply, of the thought it is possible to grasp the letter, as we will show; but of the dark saying, not even such a thing; for example also that in Isaiah: Woe, wings of a land of ships, beyond rivers of Ethiopia, sending hostages in the sea and papyrus letters upon the water. To clarify each of these and to grasp it as lighting up its darkness by the interpretation is not of the present occasion, lest we make many and untimely digressions. It is enough only to clarify somehow the saying from the psalm. For as much as I had cried out hymning God, and through the whole day speaking theology, nothing of mine was growing old, but as much as I was being renewed. But when, having been idle from saying the things of theology, I was silent, then the oldness sank in as far as my bones, and the things seeming firmest in me. And to these there followed Your hand becoming heavy night and day against me, and for this reason from the former oversight your hand weighted against me was turned into my misery. And worthily I have suffered these things, a thorn having been fixed for me when I was held by cares, or also by wealth, and by pleasures of life. And that such things have been understood by the Prophet in these is clear from what is brought on: I made known my sin, and the things following. After these it is possible to see what the sayings of the wise are; then what the riddles are; of which wise men the sayings the wise man who has heard these, and through having heard them becoming wiser than himself. pass_b_english: …very wisely written, because the crowds could not gather to him, but only those who stood apart from the crowds — his disciples — who could speak freely enough to enter Jesus house. There, not as people outside but able to be inside, they come to the teacher and ask to learn the inner sense of the parables. Because they could follow him as he went into the house, he answered Explain the parable to us with what he said.

Jesus does not only leave his house so that, standing outside, he may speak parables to those outside; he also sits beside the sea, hinting that the crowds and the outsiders are not far from the sea waves and its salt water. Watch this: many crowds gathered to Jesus who had left the house and sat by the sea; yet it is no longer many crowds, but the few who travel the narrow, hard road and find the way that leads to life — disciples — who enter to him into the house.

Testing what fits a gospel word as far as I can, and Jesus purpose when he stepped into the boat and spoke in parables to the whole crowd on the shore, I say: perhaps the Word, not having planted a foot and not standing, but being in sea water, speaks as he is carried on what can, as far as possible, stand on water — and that is called a boat. Do not be surprised if such thoughts are brought in with more beauty, so that the outsider and the crowd will not think there is no hidden mind at all, dense and elegant, stored for the gospel disposition; for that too was a work of the grace that manages God Word.

I also try to hear more deeply: The disciples came and said, Why do you speak to them in parables? and Leaving the crowds he came into his house; and his disciples came saying, Explain the parable to us. Crowds who hear a parable never even pause over it as needing explanation. Disciples see that he speaks in parables to crowds because they are outside; they follow Jesus as he leaves the crowds; they see they can learn the parables nowhere else than by entering Jesus house; so they enter, come to him, and say, Explain to us the parable we want to learn. That is the parable.

Next is the dark saying. In the Scriptures some things are said so deliberately dark that no one can catch even a casual sense in them without much hard examination — muddled in phrasing, in thought, and in how the wording is put together. I take that to be what a book calls a dark saying. An example from the Psalms, from Psalm 32: Because I was silent, my bones grew old, and what follows. Of ordinary thought you can grasp the letter, as we will show; of a dark saying, not even that. Compare Isaiah: Woe, wings of a land of ships beyond the rivers of Ethiopia, sending hostages by sea and papyrus letters on the water. Clarifying each of these and lighting its darkness by interpretation is not for this moment, lest we digress too far. It is enough to clarify the psalm saying somehow. As long as I cried out hymning God and spoke of God all day, nothing in me grew old; I was being made new. But when I fell idle from theology and was silent, oldness sank as far as my bones and what seemed firmest in me. Then followed Your hand heavy on me night and day, and so from earlier oversight your weighted hand was turned into my misery. I deserved it: a thorn was fixed in me when cares, or wealth, or life pleasures held me. That the prophet meant this is clear from what follows: I made known my sin, and so on.
